transcript:
Header: 2028-09-08 15:00 UTC — Duration 62 minutes
Attendees: Maeve Ortiz (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Lema (Helixoria - Head of ML), Jonas Kramer (VP Eng), Priya Desai (SRE), Evan Truong (Prod Ops), Lina Morales (Security)
---
00:00 Maeve Ortiz: okay hey everyone thanks for carving out the time we wanted to do a quick operational handoff, make sure the pilot timeline looks good and surface any last blockers, uh i'm maeve from redwood.
00:12 Sofia Lema: thanks maeve yeah appreciate it, we've been looking forward to this. quick note, i'm Sofia, i'll own model validation on our side.
00:18 Jonas Kramer: Jonas here, i care about rollout and chaos resilience.
00:23 Ravi Patel: ravi, redwood se — i'll be running the perf tests and the integration pieces.
00:29 Priya Desai: priya, SRE — firewall/vpc questions mostly.
:36 Evan Truong: evan, product ops, i'll be coordinating observability.
00:40 Lina Morales: lina in security, SOC2 and KMS questions.
---
01:05 Maeve Ortiz: high level, goal is a 6-week pilot: ingest production-ish traffic to test latency / cost / degradations, prove our KV prefix caching reduces token cost at p95, and validate routing fallback behavior. are we aligned on that as the success criteria?
01:23 Sofia Lema: that's right; specifically we need p99 tail below 450ms for short prompts and averaged 20% cost reduction on inference per-session after batching and caching. those are our thresholds.
01:41 Jonas Kramer: and from infra we need a playbook if latency spikes, we can't have a cascade of retries. what do you do at 99.9th percentile failure?
01:56 Ravi Patel: good call. so redwood runtime has an automatic fallback policy — we'll route to a slightly cheaper variant when queue depth grows, and we also have a degraded quality fallback to a smaller quantized model. we'll share the exact policy we'll use during the pilot.
02:18 Priya Desai: can you explain the VPC options again — peering vs private deployment package, we need to pick.
02:29 Maeve Ortiz: short answer: hosted + VPC peering is fastest to stand up — you get private networking to our control plane with traffic over peering, keys still in our KMS if you choose hosted. private deployment (customer-managed control plane) gives you full data isolation and your KMS/HSM. there's a middle ground for dedicated where keys can be customer-managed, depending on contract.
02:53 Lina Morales: we need KMS with customer key control and strict audit logs for all token-level operations. SOC2 docs alone won't cut it; we need encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys.
03:08 Maeve Ortiz: noted — we'll attach an addendum that covers KMS options and audit log retention. we can support BYOK for dedicated and private deploy.
---
03:45 Ravi Patel: on perf, we ran a 48-hour staging run simulating your session distribution that sofia sent. results show median 60ms, p95 around 280ms on the hosted profile, and cost per 1k tokens approximately 0.84 USD with default batching. with prefix KV caching enabled, we saw cost drop to 0.67 USD for the same workload. caveat: cache effectiveness depends on session reuse and prompt overlap.
04:10 Sofia Lema: interesting — our real traffic has a lot of similar system prompts but the free-text queries vary. what hit rate did you see?
04:21 Ravi Patel: on that run hit rate was 42% across sessions; when we increased prefix window it went to 57% but tail latency increased a bit on cold starts. we'll tune.
04:33 Jonas Kramer: what's the trade on increasing prefix window? does it blow memory on the GPU?
04:40 Ravi Patel: yeah it increases KV pressure; we recommend a heuristics-based windowing and TTL. the runtime will evict older KV entries to keep within a memory budget. for dedicated fleets we can provision larger KV cache sizes.
05:05 Priya Desai: firewall rules — what's needed to open for peering? we have strict egress policies.
05:13 Maeve Ortiz: minimal ports for TLS to our endpoint, plus IP ranges for peering. ravi will share the IP CIDRs. for private deployment there's no egress, it's all internal.
05:28 Priya Desai: can you send a hardened example ruleset?
05:31 Ravi Patel: yep i'll add a ruleset example to the repo.
---
06:00 Evan Truong: observability — can we get token-level cost breakdowns in your console? we want to tie costs to routes and features.
06:09 Maeve Ortiz: yes console provides token-level breakdown by route/model, plus trace links. retention on the hosted plan is 90 days by default; we can increase retention under enterprise add-on.
06:23 Evan Truong: good, send screenshots.
---
06:45 Lina Morales: security deep dive — how do you handle audit logs, SAML/SSO, RBAC?
06:53 Maeve Ortiz: SAML SSO is supported with SCIM provisioning. RBAC is role-based in the console with granular scopes; audit logs are immutable for the retention window and include token-level operation events. for private deployments logs can be shipped to your SIEM.
07:15 Lina Morales: we need multiregion log replication and tamper-evident storage for critical audits.
07:23 Maeve Ortiz: that's possible in the private deployment; we'll capture requirements in the security checklist.
---
07:40 Sofia Lema: okay now about costs — you said dedicated lowers per-token cost; how do you model committed capacity?
07:50 Maeve Ortiz: dedicated is a reservation model: you commit to a throughput tier with monthly billing, and the unit cost per-token drops ~20–40% depending on the GPU profile and quantization. we provided a baseline estimate in the preliminary pricing doc; i'll send an updated variant that maps to your traffic percentiles.
08:10 Jonas Kramer: can you show a blended model where we start hosted then transition to dedicated as volume ramps?
08:18 Ravi Patel: absolutely — we have routing policies to siphon traffic based on rate and latency SLOs, plus an automated canary rollout. you can pin sessions to hosted or dedicated during migration windows. we'll demo this in the pilot.
---
09:05 Priya Desai: about rollback, if a model roll out regresses on quality, what's the immediate mitigation?
09:12 Ravi Patel: automatic fallback to the previous pinned model, plus a canary threshold that pauses rollout if certain metrics cross. you can also configure instant route-level failover to a different region.
09:25 Jonas Kramer: how long does a rollback take?
09:28 Ravi Patel: typical propagation is seconds for routing changes; model load times depend on model size but we keep warm instances for common models to reduce cold start to under 10s.
---
10:12 Maeve Ortiz: security/doc ask — lina we will schedule a focused meeting next week to review KMS/HSM key control and audit log formats, is thursday 9/14 OK?
10:20 Lina Morales: thursday works.
10:22 Maeve Ortiz: great. i'll invite.
---
11:05 Sofia Lema: one more technical — the KV cache eviction policy, can we have visibility into per-session KV hit/miss metrics?
11:12 Ravi Patel: yes, we emit cache metrics to the console and via prom metrics in dedicated/private. for hosted we'll surface aggregated hit/miss; for dedicated you can get per-fleet granular metrics.
11:28 Sofia Lema: perfect, that's critical for our quality/cost analysis.
---
12:00 Evan Truong: timeline and gating — we want to run the pilot starting 2028-09-20 for six weeks, are you able to support that?
12:07 Maeve Ortiz: yes, that fits. action items: share finalized pricing and pilot SOW by 9/10, security deep dive 9/14, initial perf experiment 9/12, and production traffic profile from helixoria by 9/11.
12:22 Jonas Kramer: if the perf experiment shows tail issues we'll want a short stress window to validate autoscale. can we get that?
12:29 Ravi Patel: yes we can schedule a stress window during week 1 of the pilot.
---
13:02 Priya Desai: question on data residency — some EU customers need tokens and logs to remain in eu-west, do you support region pinning?
13:11 Maeve Ortiz: yes, region pinning is supported in dedicated and private; for hosted we have EU regions and can keep data and logs in-region but we'll surface specifics in the addendum.
---
13:40 Lina Morales: any contractual items we should flag? indemnities, data deletion SLA?
13:48 Maeve Ortiz: we'll include standard data deletion windows and an SLA for deletion on offboarding; indemnities we'll route through legal but we can attach standard enterprise clauses.
---
14:10 Ravi Patel: quick demo pointer — i'll drop a link to the perf dashboard that maps p50/p95/p99 to cost buckets and will include the KV cache experiment run results.
14:22 Maeve Ortiz: and i'll attach the pricing spreadsheet with blended hosted/dedicated scenarios and the proposed pilot SOW.
---
14:44 Sofia Lema: recap: we'll send traffic profile by 9/11; redwood shares pricing and SOW by 9/10; security deep dive 9/14; perf run and test harness by 9/12. Pilot start 9/20 for six weeks. if those dates move we'll update the thread.
14:58 Maeve Ortiz: great, thanks everyone. any last minute?
15:03 Jonas Kramer: no, thanks.
15:05 Lina Morales: thanks, see you on 9/14.
15:08 Maeve Ortiz: end meeting.
---
